title: Installation and project setup
summary: Set up an external npm project, use the browser CDN, or prepare the documentation runtime.

blocks.text: Choose your setup

Use Retiam as an npm library in your own project, load it through CDN modules, or export a finished scene as an independent embed. The main workflow in these guides is authoring an animation in an external npm project and generating a video. Running this documentation site is a separate repository task.

cells: Write scenes in your own TypeScript project; the main workflow is generating animation videos.
Scene source, rendered video and snapshots
Load the engine directly in a browser, as the documentation’s live examples do.
A browser page that imports Retiam from a module URL
Publish a finished scene on another website.
An exported web component and its bundled assets, without a separate Retiam installation or engine CDN

blocks.text: 1. Install Retiam in your own npm project

Create a project for your animations. Your scene imports the public package instead of reaching into the engine’s source tree. Core types come from retiam; specialized libraries use entry points such as retiam/charts, retiam/physics and retiam/shapes.

blocks.code:
mkdir my-retiam-animation
cd my-retiam-animation
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm install retiam
npm install --save-dev typescript vite @webgpu/types
npm pkg set scripts.dev="vite" scripts.check="tsc --noEmit"

blocks.text: If you are working with an unpublished engine checkout, build it and run npm pack in the engine repository, then install that tarball in this project instead of the registry package. The project layout and package imports stay the same.

blocks.text: Save this as tsconfig.json so TypeScript can check the scene, browser entry and WebGPU types.

Save the scene below as scenes/MyScene.ts. Its four-second sequence reveals a circle, moves it, holds briefly and fades it out. Durations are milliseconds; the same scene can be previewed and rendered without changing its choreography.
Save the canvas host as index.html. The CSS gives the canvas a real display size; the composer sets its drawing resolution for browser preview or CLI output.

Save this as `vite.config.ts`. Retiam ships a split ESM bundle whose font and other assets are resolved relative to its modules. Exclude it from Vite dependency prebundling so those URLs stay at the package location. The render and snapshot CLI also load this configuration from the consumer project.

blocks.code:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <title>My Retiam animation</title>
    <style>
      html, body { margin: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; }
      canvas { display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <canvas id="canvas"></canvas>
    <script type="module" src="/src/main.ts"></script>
  </body>
</html>

blocks.text: Save this entry as src/main.ts. It loads a default-exported Scene class from the file query parameter, so the CLI can choose your scene. Scene.start creates the composer, whose initialization reads the CLI’s offline rendering settings.

blocks.code:
npm run check
npm run dev

blocks.text: Open the local URL printed by Vite to preview the animation. Next, follow [video rendering](/export#cli-preview-and-final-render) for the CLI dependencies, output settings and render command. The current render and snapshot commands serve this project’s index.html, so keep the host and file selection entry alongside your scenes.
2. Load Retiam from a CDN

Load the built ES module directly in a browser when you want a live scene without installing Retiam in that page. This is how the documentation’s editable examples load the engine. The current local engine server is http://localhost:3000; the import URL is http://localhost:3000/retiam.es.js.

Serve this HTML over HTTP locally. An import map lets JavaScript scene modules use the same package names as npm projects; add only the sublibrary mappings your scene needs. A browser page uses JavaScript modules, so transpile TypeScript before loading it directly. The documentation editor provides that compilation for its live examples.

For a published page, replace the local server URLs with a versioned npm CDN URL. Serve the engine’s emitted assets and sublibrary bundles with the module, and enable CORS for the page’s origin. [Documentation authoring](/docs-authoring#engine-cdn) explains that configuration.
3. Export an independent embedded scene

Export packages a finished scene with the engine code it needs into a web component. The receiving site serves the exported JavaScript and assets; it can run the scene without installing Retiam or importing a separate engine CDN. Use this when sharing the animation itself as an interactive scene on a website.

Continue with the [npm embed recipe](/export#embed-from-npm) for a complete package-based component entry, build configuration and receiving page. The [repository export CLI](/export#standalone-embeds) has separate setup requirements. Keep any emitted assets with the bundle. Fonts, videos, models or services referenced by remote URLs remain runtime dependencies until the scene packages or localizes them.
Browser and asset requirements

Retiam needs a working WebGPU device and a canvas with non-zero dimensions. Both npm and CDN scenes execute in a browser context that exposes navigator.gpu, such as localhost or a suitable secure origin. Video rendering uses a headless browser with those same GPU requirements. The current Box3D backend uses the single-threaded standard WebAssembly build, so it does not require COOP/COEP and can run on static hosts such as GitHub Pages. A future threaded WebAssembly feature would require a host that serves the necessary isolation headers.

A consumer bundler must resolve package exports and emitted assets. Import `retiam/shapes` and the other sublibraries through their package entry points. Do not paste `../../../src` imports from a repository demo into an unrelated application.

blocks.content: Avoid hard-coded browser-version guarantees. Feature availability depends on browser build, operating system, GPU, driver and execution context. Check capabilities where the feature is used.

blocks.text: Work on the engine or documentation repository

Clone Retiam for engine or Studio development. Clone the separate retiam-docs project to maintain this documentation; its normal install, build and tests require no engine checkout. For an external npm animation project, use the setup above.
In a separate clone of retiam-docs, install its dependencies and start the documentation viewer:

The standalone retiam-docs repository prepares its own scene modules and assets, then imports Retiam from cdnUrl in content/config.json. Run npm ci and npm run dev in that project. The local engine URL remains http://localhost:3000/retiam.es.js; run that CDN separately when needed. GitHub Pages builds use a pinned published HTTPS URL in the same configuration file. Optional speech and model services are configured under services in that file and hosted separately.
Builds and entry points

`npm run build` runs TypeScript and Vite. The core bundle is `dist/retiam.es.js`; library bundles are `dist/libs/<name>/index.js`. Declarations live under `dist/src` and `dist/libs`. The root barrel `src/index.ts` is generated; change source modules rather than hand-editing the barrel.
Exact contracts: [Scene](/api-core-scene#scene), [SceneComposer](/api-core-scenecomposer#scenecomposer), [RenderConfig](/api-render#renderconfig).
